s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Patient is taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Platelet count is within normal range
Prothrombin time is slightly elevated
Activated partial thromboplastin time is elevated
Serum zinc level is low
Biopsy from left groin showed subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
Direct immunofluorescence test was negative
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive painful blisters and ulcers with subepidermal blistering and association with multiple myeloma

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and presence of apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining

shortlist.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Low serum zinc level and presence of skin lesions and ulcers

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blistering and presence of chronic inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blistering and presence of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining are consistent with amyloidosis, which is a known complication of multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: The direct immunofluorescence test was negative, which is not typical for paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
rejected.why: While the patient has a low serum zinc level, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not primarily suggest a zinc deficiency disorder.

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not align with bullous pemphigoid, which typically shows linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone on direct immunofluorescence.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of a history of skin fragility or blistering at other times in her life make this diagnosis less likely.
